You are sworn to uphold the law of Ardent and you carry the king's authority over all. The king has been petitioned to stop a series of abductions occuring in the villages of Benston and Pirn. A proctor was sent before you, but she has not reported back and is considered missing.

You are a cobbler of notable skill from the village of Pirn. From time to time you travel to nearby villages in an effort to expand your market. On the latest such occasion you were ambushed during your trip. Your assailants appear to have no interest in your goods, they abducted you without giving reason.

Augmenting strikes by swinging and moving your body can greatly increase damage.
Your character is subject to physics, your inputs must work in harmony with them.
Even when a parry is not successful, attempting to defend will reduce damage taken.
Let go of LMB at any time to perform a feint or abandon your attack to defend instead.
To successfully block or parry you must turn and position yourself to face the blow.
NPCs play by the same exact rules, make human errors and have slow reaction times.

Overhead attacks can deliver devastating head blows and hit prone opponents.
Slash damage is effective on weak and slicing blows but easily mitigated by armour.
Piercing damage is better at finding potential gaps and weak spots in armour.
Crushing damage is reliant on strong blows but typically most effective against armour.
Weapons with a higher balance are quicker and more responsive.
Impact mainly deals stamina damage but also affects all other damage types.
Armour can be worn in layers for even better protection.
Higher coverage armour has fewer exposed parts and weaknesses.

This is your base of operations and living space.[tcol=FFE399]Manage[/tcol] your company by clicking on the board on our left.Directly ahead is a [tcol=FFE399]Shop[/tcol] where you can buy and sell equipment.[tcol=FFE399]Matches[/tcol] that you can participate in are accessed from the board on your right.
The inventory shows items you are currently wearing and carrying.Items you wear while outside of a match are not carried into matches. To equip items for combat you must use the management screen.

Matches are split into three main categories.[tcol=FFE399]Standard[/tcol] matches can be run at any time and configured to your preference.[tcol=FFEF99]Specials[/tcol] change daily and can only be run when and as available.[tcol=FFE399]Tournaments[/tcol] are weekly multiple match events where fighting companies compete for important prizes.Select a match and then enter your fighters by dragging them to the right. Some matches require multiple participants.[tcol=FFE399]Rank[/tcol] is a requirement, your fighter must attain this rank before they can participate.[tcol=FFE399]Tier[/tcol] indicates the level of equipment used in the match. This corresponds to your loadouts in the manage screen.

This is where you can buy and sell items.Drag items you want to buy from the shop's stock to the right pane, items you want to sell go in the left pane.You can try items on before you buy them by dragging them on to the paperdoll.Note that rank restrictions are applied to some items. You must achieve that rank and participate in appropriate matches to use these.Invest early and invest wisely, even a few basic layers of clothing can offer great protection from injury.

[tcol=FFE399]Manage[/tcol] equipment and training for your roster.The [tcol=FFE399]Arsenal[/tcol] allows you to organise your equipment.[tcol=FFE399]Recruit[/tcol] new fighters to control in battle.[tcol=FFE399]Hire[/tcol] combatants for team matches and other staff.Daily [tcol=FFE399]report[/tcol] items can be double clicked to take action.

Fighters gain a [tcol=FFE399]rank[/tcol] every two skill techniques learnt.Each rank has a corresponding loadout. Which loadout is used depends on the tier of the match. Use the slider to select a ranked loadout.[tcol=FFE399]Point[/tcol] limits are also applied to each rank. Every item carries a point cost.

Tournaments are held weekly. Fighting companies compete in each tournament for a prize. If a company wins all four tournaments in a season they are awarded an exclusive suit of armour.You must enter fighters in advance of the tournament day; once the tournament is in progress you will not be able to enter or remove fighters. Only master rank fighters are eligible to participate in tournaments.To win a tournament you must win at least three of the six events. It is advisable to enter different fighters in as many events as you can to improve your chances of winning.

This book presents itself as nothing more than a collection of absurd theories on the existence of ghosts, however there are parts written in a different tone.

"There is an innate power in the ghost realm, unlike the physical world it is not governed by the constraints of matter or the laws of physics. A ghost can conjure anything, any object or power they can simply call into being, much as we do when we dream. This however requires keen awareness of their condition, an understanding of their realm and their place within it. Most ghosts wander in a state of confusion, at the mercy of twisted thoughts and perceptions, but not all. There are those that have awakened, or perhaps never slept, never were in a dream like state. These wield great power, they can shape things not only in the ghost realm but within our own."

Life of Linus Fendrick by Anonymous.

A famous book with an even more famous story surrounding it, often told by mothers to their young children, a cautionary tale on the dark and sinister trappings of thaumaturgy. Fendrick was a gifted thaumaturge who lost his young wife and three children in some gruesome accident. He was thus driven to necromancy in the hope of resurrecting them, not the traditional crude raising of the dead, but with full sentience and cognizance. His practices and experiments were most vile in nature. Kidnappings, torture, murder, keeping his family's bodies in a state between life and death for some forty years; his crimes were plentiful and led to nothing save failure and despair.

A medical book on human anatomy. Mostly complex diagrams and surgical terminology. There are many underlined passages and circled diagrams in the section that deals with the brain.

The Forgotten Power by Anonymous

According to this book humans are powerful, immortal beings that have forgotten their true nature. That, by living your life by a certain moral code, performing certain rituals and eating a certain diet, you can achieve great power and ultimately unlock your dormant immortality.

Forgotten by Aime Koren.

A scholarly book about memory and cognizance. What we forget and why we forget it, how we choose to make a history for ourselves regardless of the facts, how we are defined by the wholly unreliable and subjective thing we call memory.

This book explores various myths surrounding the Guardian but does so in what seems like a tendentious manner, casting him in a more positive light than he is commonly viewed in. You suspect it is tied to some cult dedicated to the worship of the Guardian.

The Guardian of the Underworld, known also as the Keeper of the Dead, is the most prominent figure in our mythology. As with most our myths it differs depending on whom you ask, the Guardian's role in particular is an ambivalent one. There is fear of what he represents and of his dark and dangerous realm but there is also a feeling of deference and a belief that he will watch over our loved ones once they pass away. We inter our dead to consign them to the Guardian's care and we believe that he will grant them a life beyond this one. Behind the intimidating titles and malicious curses the Guardian is also a giver of life. He is said to restore life to those that have fallen in his service, or that some become beholden to him owing to their resurrection. Perhaps the most notable myth is that in a time of dire need the Guardian will raise an army of those given into his care to defend us. What is it then that he guards? Does he simply watch over our dead and his dreadful realm or might it be that he is in fact our protector?

The Earth on which we walk is our mother, she provides for us all that we may need. Our ancestors, in their mad lust for power sought more, they began to dig deep into our Earth, in search of her lifeblood. And so by digging they uncovered the Underworld and its fearsome Guardian. He sent forth terrible demons to drive them out and hunt them down. Before all could be slain, our ancient kin sealed the entrances to the Underworld and swore never to return. Thus are we allowed to live upon this Earth, but ever under the watchful eye of the Guardian.
